summary: The Phoenix proposal successfully meets the outlined constraints and objectives, allowing local agents to exchange immutable snapshots and typed research signals without altering production weights or verdicts. The implementation ensures safety and backward compatibility.
top_technical_reasons: Events are append-only, hash-linked, and replayable, ensuring data integrity.
Unsafe events are rejected, maintaining system safety.
Agent signals are enriched with necessary metadata, enhancing traceability and research capabilities.
The existing AgentDirector output remains backward compatible, ensuring no disruption to current operations.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Increasing the number of agents will not affect the deterministic replay of events.
next_experiments.change: Introduce additional agents to the system.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Monitor the consistency of event replay across multiple agents.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: This will test the scalability of the event bus and ensure that performance remains stable with increased complexity.

next_experiments.hypothesis: The rejection of unsafe events will not impact the overall throughput of the event processing.
next_experiments.change: Simulate a high volume of events, including both safe and unsafe.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Measure the processing time and throughput of events.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: This will help assess the efficiency of the safety checks and their impact on system performance.

data_or_label_risks: Minimal, as the proposal adheres to strict safety protocols and does not alter production weights or verdicts.
